hooks.text: A rushed political deadline forced the world's largest airship skyward.
Britain's proudest new flying machine was actually an untested deathtrap.
Why did Britain's Air Minister board an untested giant airship?

title: Why Did Britain's Giant R101 Airship Crash? ⚠️
description: The tragic story of the R101, Britain's giant imperial airship that crashed in France on its maiden voyage in 1930.

beats.text: A rushed political deadline forced the world's largest airship skyward.
beats.visual: photograph of the R101 airship at its mooring mast, 1930

beats.text: In October 1930, Britain's R101 departed for India on its maiden voyage.
beats.visual: photograph of R101 airship flying over London, 1930

beats.text: To boost lift, designers had hastily sliced in an extra gas cell.
beats.visual: photograph of the interior structure of R101 showing gasbag, 1929

beats.text: Air Minister Lord [Thomson](/tˈɑmsˈʌn/) boarded despite storm warnings and missed trials.
beats.visual: portrait photograph of Christopher Thomson, 1st Baron Thomson, 1929

beats.text: Gales over France forced the giant into two steep, fatal dives.
beats.visual: photograph of the metal wreckage of R101 on a hillside near Beauvais, 1930

beats.text: The hydrogen ignited instantly, killing forty-eight people inside the blazing hull.
beats.visual: photograph of the burned skeleton of the R101 airship, 1930

beats.text: The only survivors were engineers riding in external engine cars.
beats.visual: photograph of an engine car suspended below an airship, 1930

beats.text: Yet the empire demanded a triumph, ignoring every warning.
beats.visual: photograph of the Royal Air Force ensign from R101 displayed in Cardington Church, 1930
